- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.1) — model tends to overshoot in bullish periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially < -0.3) — model underreacts to bearish sentiment.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast if recent sentiment is mixed or negative — model often overcorrects after short-term rallies.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Lagged response: if sentiment turns negative after forecast peak, reduce forecast by 2–5% per day of lag.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic when sentiment is volatile — cap forecast at 10% above 30-day moving average.
- Don’t assume sentiment directly translates to price — if sentiment is high but price is flat, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence.
